target_customer: Early on wealthy buyers of jetpacks and a flying motorcycle; later national defense, cargo, firefighting and disaster relief customers
problem: Personal vertical flight without rotors, so that a small, fast vehicle could operate in urban areas and carry cargo.
business_model: Aircraft and jetpack sales with pre-orders, later government and defense development

founders.name: David Mayman
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page; coverage calls him CEO of Mayman Aerospace. No bio opened.

founders.name: Boris Jarry
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page; no bio.

competitors.name: Gravity Industries
competitors.what: Wearable jet suit rather than a hoverbike
competitors.traction_then: Reported jet suit patent granted 14 March 2019 and a planned race series

technical_complexity.rationale: Rotor-free jet-powered VTOL with heavy lift needs propulsion, control and safety work and eventual aviation certification.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary jet and control engineering and certification effort are barriers, but the market is tiny and few buyers exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No large incumbent was building the same wedge; Gravity Industries and Martin Aircraft were small players.

market_need_then: Demand was speculative and tied to novelty buyers and niche government uses. The Speeder was open for pre-order at $380,000 in March 2019 per press.

identity.voice_and_tone: Bold with the tagline Flying motorcycles

branding.brand_signature: Flying motorcycles tagline and the Speeder name

rebrands.why: CEO said the JetPack name served the jetpack technology but a brand was needed that defined professional markets such as defense, cargo, firefighting and disaster relief
CEO said too many things were calling themselves Speeder

branding.community_and_virality: Widely covered by consumer press (Robb Report, New Atlas, Yahoo, RideApart) for the flying motorcycle.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong media attention for a vivid concept, but the JetPack name was later judged too narrow and the product name was changed twice.

pivots.to: Autonomous high-speed VTOL drone called Razor for the military market
pivots.why: Per Robb Report, a temporary pivot to defense; the jetpack was to be discontinued

outcome_analysis: JetPack Aviation, now Mayman Aerospace, built flying prototypes and raised a $2M seed in November 2019 and $3M from the UAE Strategic Development Fund in February 2023. By April 2024 it pivoted toward military drones and planned to discontinue the jetpack, with a crewed version not expected before 2028. It remains active but capital is small for certification-heavy aircraft.
notes: The seed round is stated by Yahoo/TechCrunch coverage and RideApart; the SDF round is stated by its own press release plus WAM and AviTrader. A 2017 StartEngine raise (about $248K) and a 2016 Seedrs campaign appeared in search results from one outlet each and are unverified, not recorded. One profile gives $2.3M total across 3 rounds. The Gravity Industries source date is inferred from the 14 March 2019 patent date mentioned in the article. Founder employers and education were not found in an opened source. The 2019 seed date is November 2019 per TechCrunch, after the Winter 2019 batch.
